sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Smithtown, and who sets the amount?
sections.html:
The Town of Smithtown Receiver of Taxes collects every real property tax levied by the town, Suffolk County and the school districts, yet sets no rate. The Department of Assessment values each parcel, and the elected boards of the school districts, county, town, villages and fire districts decide how much money they need.

The assessor's office compares the levy to a pie: the levy is the whole pie, and your assessment fixes only how large a slice you carry. In most cases the school district tax is the biggest portion of a bill, and it follows the budget residents vote on each May.

sections.h2: When are Smithtown property taxes due?
sections.html:
Smithtown's tax year begins December 1 and ends November 30. One bill is mailed around mid-December, and owners may settle it whole or in two halves. The receiver states that neither date carries a grace period.

Smithtown property tax calendar (source: Town of Smithtown Receiver of Taxes)
DateWhat happens
December 1Tax year begins
Mid-DecemberSingle annual bill mailed
January 10First half due without penalty
May 31Second half due without penalty (June 1 for 2026)
After May 31Payments go to Suffolk County
November 30Tax year ends

The June 1 extension applied to the 2026 bill and has passed. Partial payments are taken from $200 up, with penalties applied only to what remains after the due date. Nothing postmarked after May 31 is accepted at the town office, and after that cutoff taxes are payable to the Suffolk County Comptroller.

sections.h2: How do you pay a Smithtown tax bill?
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes works from 99 W. Main Street, with the payment window closing at 4:30 p.m. and summer hours ending earlier, at 4 p.m. The options are:

  • Online, by credit card or e-check, with a service fee added.
  • By phone through the automated line published on the town page, also with a fee.
  • By mail. Enclose the whole current bill to get a receipt, and write the district, section, block and lot on the check.
  • At Town Hall, by check, money order, cash or credit card. Debit cards carry a $3.95 fee.
  • In the drop box at the side entrance of Town Hall.

The office phone is (631) 360-7610.

sections.h2: How does Smithtown assess property, and how do you appeal?
sections.html:
The Department of Assessment sets each property's fair market value. An owner who agrees that the figure matches what a sale would bring needs do nothing, and one who disagrees uses the grievance process. Grievance Day falls on the third Tuesday of May.

Exemptions run on another clock. Applications must reach the department by 5:00 p.m. on March 1, though a STAR application only needs a postmark of that day, and a weekend March 1 pushes the deadline to Monday. An approved exemption shows on the next December bill. Denial letters are mailed by May 1, which leaves time to grieve before Grievance Day.

A cut won through a small claims petition normally appears on the tax bill. If it arrives late in the year, the second half may be adjusted, and if that is too late Suffolk County refunds the owner directly. The assessor's office is at (631) 360-7560. The assessor's list of reasons a bill rises:

  • A higher rate set by a taxing district.
  • A higher assessed value.
  • An exemption that lapsed or was never renewed.
  • A new owner who does not qualify for the seller's exemption.

sections.h2: What do federal statistics show for Smithtown?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 116,847 people, against 116,296 counted in April 2020. About 88.7 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, and 95 percent of residents did not move in the last year.

  • Households, 2020 to 2024: 39,611, averaging 2.87 people.
  • Typical value of an owned home: $669,900.
  • Typical monthly cost for owners with a mortgage: $3,809.
  • Typical gross rent: $2,233.
  • Typical household income in 2024 dollars: $152,636.
  • Average trip to work: 32.2 minutes.

Because a lapsed exemption is one reason bills climb, confirm yours is current before you pick a closing date.

sections.h2: Where is Smithtown, and what communities does it include?
sections.html:
Smithtown occupies the North Shore of Long Island. Long Island Sound lies to its north, Islip to the south, Brookhaven to the east and Huntington to the west. Its 111.5 square miles of total area include 53.8 of land. The Nicolls Patent of 1665, granted to Richard Smith, is taken as the founding date.

Three villages are incorporated within the town: Head of the Harbor, Nissequogue and the Village of the Branch. The hamlets are Smithtown, Kings Park, St. James and Nesconset, along with parts of Commack, Fort Salonga, Hauppauge and Lake Ronkonkoma, several shared with neighboring towns.

Six school districts reach into Smithtown: Smithtown Central, Kings Park Central, Commack, Hauppauge, Sachem and Three Village. The Long Island Rail Road's Port Jefferson Branch stops at Kings Park, Smithtown and St. James. Several of the districts straddle town lines, so read the district name printed on your bill.

Getting around is mostly by car or rail. Suffolk County Transit buses serve the whole town, and the main roads are:

  • NY 25 (Jericho Turnpike and Main Street) and NY 25A, which cross at the Smithtown Bull.
  • NY 111, the main north to south state route, and NY 347, known as the Smithtown Bypass.
  • The Northern State Parkway and the Sunken Meadow State Parkway, with the Long Island Expressway touching only the southwest corner.

Caleb Smith State Park Preserve, Sunken Meadow State Park and Nissequogue River State Park lie within the town, and the town's board meetings are broadcast on its public service television station.

sections.h2: What should you settle before selling a Smithtown house?
sections.html:
Begin with the receiver. Request the amount currently due on your parcel, since neither half has a grace period and unpaid balances after May 31 move to Suffolk County. The tax map number appears on the bill, and the receiver asks for the district, section, block and lot on any mailed check.

Then visit the Building Department at 23 Redwood Lane. It enforces the State building code and the town's zoning, issues permits and certificates of occupancy, and searches its records without charge to see whether each permit has a matching certificate. Work done without a permit will not have one. A home built before permits began in 1947 can request a History Letter. Duplicate certificates with a raised seal are sold for a fee, inspections are booked at (631) 360-7522, and the department does not take applications inside the Village of the Branch, Nissequogue or Head of the Harbor.

Permit triggers the department lists:

  • Pools able to hold water deeper than 24 inches, with a 4 to 6 foot fence or self-latching gate.
  • Fences over four feet tall.
  • Detached sheds over 144 square feet and 12 feet tall, and other accessory structures over 50 square feet.
  • A wider window opening or changed header, and any skylight.
  • New gables or a changed roof pitch, though not simple re-shingling.
  • Decks more than 8 inches above grade.

Deeds are filed with the Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead. On a $669,900 sale the state's base transfer tax is $2,680, computed on $670,000, and the seller pays it unless the contract says otherwise.

faqs.q: When is the first half of the Smithtown tax bill due?
faqs.a: By January 10, without penalty. The bill goes out once a year in mid-December, and the receiver says there is no grace period.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Smithtown taxes after May 31?
faqs.a: To Suffolk County. The Receiver of Taxes cannot take payments postmarked after May 31.

faqs.q: What is the smallest partial payment Smithtown takes?
faqs.a: $200. Penalties apply only to the balance left after the due date.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Smithtown?
faqs.a: The third Tuesday of May. Exemption denials are mailed by May 1, which leaves time to file.

faqs.q: What is the Smithtown exemption application deadline?
faqs.a: The Department of Assessment must have the application by 5:00 p.m. on March 1, though STAR applications may be postmarked that day. A weekend date moves the deadline to Monday.
